newsitem.title: FRANCE: France vows to stand firm against Corsica violence.
newsitem.headline: France vows to stand firm against Corsica violence.

text.p: French Defence Minister Charles Millon renewed a government pledge on Thursday to stand firm against separatist violence on Corsica, just hours after petrol bomb attacks on two island gendarmerie barracks.
"The government will not yield. Rather than weaken, we must continue our efforts to assure public order," Millon said during a visit to the French Mediterranean resort island.
One of the first sites he visited was an island gendarmerie which separatists seeking greater autonomy from mainland France have sprayed with bullets on several occasions .

After chatting with some of the paramilitary gendarmes and their families as well as local officials, Millon said security would be stepped up at the gendarmeries to better protect those who worked there.
Corsica has been rocked by two decades of low-level separatist guerrilla warfare. The government has vowed to crack down on the violence but many of the guerrillas are apparently undeterred.
Over the past eight months, gendarmeries have reported some 40 machine-gun attacks.

Just hours before Millon's arrival, suspected separatists threw petrol bombs at gendarmerie barracks in Porto-Vecchio and Figari in southern Corsica, damaging the barracks and three nearby cars but causing no injuries.

Separatist sympathisers had demonstrated outside the Porto-Vecchio barracks to protest at the detention of three people in an investigation into a bombing and alleged extortion attempt at the Sperone golf course in December.
Police said on Wednesday they had detained a total of 10 people for questioning in connection with the golf course probe.
Three of those in custody were suspected of being intermediaries in the alleged scheme to extort protection money from the golf course owner by bombing it, police said.
Such payments are known in Corsica as a "revolutionary tax".
A top leader of the political wing of the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC), Francois Santoni, is already in custody in connection with the scheme.
